2_no_fatals_on_boot.evidence: BUDDYNEXT_IMPORTER_VERSION prints 1.1.0, matching the zip filename. debug.log gained 1 line, and it is WordPress core's wp_version_check() network warning (no outbound net in Docker), not ours. 0 lines matching fatal/uncaught/class-not-found/textdomain_just_in_time.

3_admin_screen_renders.evidence: Renders inside .bni-wrap, no PHP notice. Source stated plainly (BuddyBoss). Step list POPULATED - 12 domain checkboxes, not zero, which is the drift condition this step exists to catch. All four panels present: Source community, What to import, Progress, Check the migration. No alert()/confirm() in any enqueued script. Verified at 1280 and 390: no horizontal spill (docScrollWidth == innerWidth at both), .bni-hint blocks keep display:flex with a 16px marker beside the text rather than collapsing.

3a_staging_advisory.evidence: New in 1.1.0. Renders above the hero, non-dismissible, role=note. 1280: flex, bg #fdf6e7, color #7a4d05, 108px tall. 390: flex, 368px wide, 202px tall, 12px padding, no overflow.

4_rest_answers_and_refuses.evidence: In-process as admin: /stats, /domains, /status all HTTP 200. Unauthenticated POST: /step 403 buddynext_importer_forbidden, /background 403, /cleanup 403 when the required confirm param is supplied - and bni_id_map + bni_checkpoint both still exist afterwards, so it refused rather than executed. (/cleanup returns 400 for a missing param before the 403, which is WordPress validating required args first; it never executes.)

6_degrades_without_buddynext.reason: WordPress itself now refuses to deactivate BuddyNext while this plugin is active - the Plugins screen shows 'Required by: BuddyNext Importer, BuddyNext Pro' and blocks it. That is the Requires Plugins header working, and it is a stronger guarantee than the degrade path it made untestable.

caveats.summary: On docker-smoke, BuddyNext's PWA service worker claims the whole origin including /wp-admin/ and answers admin REST with the offline HTML page at HTTP 200. The importer's admin screen then shows 'Could not load source statistics.' and renders 0 of 12 domains. WordPress CORE REST is hit too - /wp/v2/users/me returns the same offline page. Server-side rest_do_request() and unauthenticated curl both return correct JSON, so the plugin is behaving; only the browser behind the SW is affected. Step 3 was therefore completed on the importer fixture, which has no service worker. Filed as its own card; does not block this release because the CLI path is unaffected and the defect is pre-existing and external.

not_proven_by_this_smoke: That a migration is CORRECT. This runbook proves install, boot, render, REST and refusal only. Correctness was established separately for 1.1.0 by real migrations against both fixtures (BuddyPress 501 users / 20 groups / 1838 activities, and BuddyBoss Platform 3.3.0), with verify and reconcile agreeing and a re-run writing 0 rows across all 18 domains.
